examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Partial Fraction Decomposition With Higher Order Factors
examples.problem:
Given that

$$
\dfrac{1-2x}{(x+1)(x+2)^3}= \dfrac{A}{x+1}+\dfrac{B}{x+2} +\dfrac{C}{(x+2)^2} + \dfrac{D}{(x+2)^3},
$$

where $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are real constants, determine the value of $AB + CD.$
examples.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)(x+2)^3$ gives

$$
1 - 2x = A(x+2)^3 + B(x+1)(x+2)^2 + C(x+1)(x+2) + D(x+1).
$$

Letting $x = -2$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2(-2) & =A(-2+2)^{3}+B(-2+1)(-2+2)^{2}+C(-2+1)(-2+2)+D(-2+1) \\ 1+4 & =-D \\ D & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x = -1$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2(-1) & =A(-1+2)^{3}+B(-1+1)(-1+2)^{2}+C(-1+1)(-1+2)+D(-1+1) \\ 1+2 & =A \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x = 0$ and using our values for $A$ and $D$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2(0) & =3(0+2)^{3}+B(0+1)(0+2)^{2}+C(0+1)(0+2)+(-5)(0+1) \\ 1-0 & =24+4B+2C-5 \\ 2C & =-4B-18 \\ C & =-2B-9.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, letting $x = 1$ and using our values for $A$ and $D$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2(1) & =A(1+2)^{3}+B(1+1)(1+2)^{2}+C(1+1)(1+2)+D(1+1) \\ 1-2 & =81+18B+6C-10 \\ 6C & =-18B-72 \\ C & =-3B-12.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

From $(1)$ and $(2)$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-2B-9 & =-3B-12 \\ B & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the value of $B$ into $(1)$  to get the value of $C{:}$

$$
C = -2(-3) - 9 = -3
$$

Finally,

$$
AB + CD = 3(-3) + (-3)(-5) = 6.
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-23x+27}{x(x-3)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x-3}+\frac{C}{(x-3)^{2}},
$$

where $A$, $B$, and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $x(x-3)^{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-23x+27=A(x-3)^{2}+Bx(x-3)+Cx.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=3$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(3)^{2}-23(3)+27 & =A(3-3)^{2}+B\cdot 3(3-3)+C\cdot 3 \\ 36-69+27 & =3C \\ -6 & =3C \\ C & =\frac{(-6)}{3} \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}-23(0)+27 & =A(0-3)^{2}+B(0)(0-3)+C(0) \\ 27 & =9A \\ A & =\frac{27}{9} \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=1$ and using our values for $A$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(1)^{2}-23(1)+27 & =3(1-3)^{2}+B(1)(1-3)+(-2)(1) \\ 4-23+27 & =12-2B-2 \\ 8 & =10-2B \\ 2B & =2 \\ B & =\frac{2}{2} \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Hence,

$$
A\cdot B\cdot C=3\cdot 1\cdot (-2)=-6.
$$
